decisions.reason: Its dedicated product page suggests a visible launch and committed development effort, and as a drainage component it fits the firm's integrated system portfolio closely enough that management would continue rather than reverse course after only one year.

A floor-level shower drainage system is highly central to the firm's stated move toward accessible, low-profile bathroom drainage, so management would be inclined to persist even with limited early evidence.

This designer shower drainage product supports the firm's promise of design-conscious solutions and was given its own page, making it both strategically important and publicly visible enough to favor continuation.

A shower element with integrated slope strengthens the firm's installation-ease and integrated-solution positioning, so management would likely justify staying with it as part of the announced direction.

The firm publicly highlighted having developed this backflow-protected basement floor drain, which creates strong commitment and a clear basis for attributing any weak start to temporary market uptake rather than product failure.

Although less prominently presented, an air-admittance valve still complements the firm's drainage know-how and compatible product families, and escalation of commitment makes an early withdrawal unlikely.
